item.title: Order continuity of induced homomorphisms between free Banach lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.00451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T\colon F\to E$ be a bounded operator between Banach spaces and let $\overline T\colon FBL^{(p)}[F]\to FBL^{(p)}[E]$ be the lattice homomorphism induced by $T$ between the corresponding free $p$-convex Banach lattices generated by $F$ and $E$. We show that $\overline T$ is order continuous if and only if it is either zero or a lattice isomorphic embedding. For $p=\infty$, this holds precisely when $T$ is zero or an isomorphic embedding, while for $1\leq p<\infty$, apart from the zero operator, $T$ must be an embedding and the pair $(T(F),E)$ must have the operator-extension property POE-$p$. In addition, we study when $FBL^{(p)}[E]$ is order dense or majorizing in $FBL^{(q)}[E]$ for $p<q$.
item.dc:creator: Ra\'ul E. Pariente-Mart\'in, Pedro Tradacete

item.title: Clarkson--McCarthy type inequalities, part II: refinements, unitary orbits, unitarily invariant norms and $\ell_s$--$\ell_s$ estimates
item.description: arXiv:2611.00459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In previous work \cite{Zha26a}, the author established Clarkson--McCarthy type inequalities for several classes of operator families, including $\ell_p$--$\ell_p$ estimates and mixed $\ell_q$--$\ell_p$ estimates, by means of operator square-sum identities. The present paper has two main aims. First, using the tracial joint spectral measures recently introduced by O.~Hein\"avaara \cite{Hei25}, we obtain several refinements of the McCarthy--Clarkson inequalities, one of which confirms a conjecture of Audenaert \cite{AK17}. Second, combining tools from matrix analysis with complex interpolation theory, we establish Clarkson--McCarthy type inequalities for unitary orbits, unitarily invariant norms, and $\ell_s$--$\ell_s$ estimates, again in the framework of operator square-sum identities.
item.dc:creator: Teng Zhang

item.title: A new perspective on Riemann surfaces and von Neumann algebras via thin Blaschke products
item.description: arXiv:2611.00933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2014, K.Guo and the second author constructed the first example of an infinite Blaschke product $B$ (a thin Blaschke product), for which the associated multiplication operator $M_B$ is irreducible on the Bergman space $L_a^2(\mathbb{D})$ over the unit disk $\mathbb D$. We take a substantial step forward toward characterizing the irreducibility of the operator $M_B$ on $L_a^2(\mathbb{D})$, or equivalently, the trivialness of the von Neumann algebra $\{M_B,M_B^*\}'$. This characterization indicates a close connection with the primeness of $B$ and with the two-component property of the Riemann surface $\mathcal{S}_B$ associated with $B$. The approach is built upon a nested family of connected components of the sublevel set $\{z\in \mathbb{D}:|B(z)|<t\}$ for $0<t<1$, which captures the function-theoretic and geometric feature of $B$.
item.dc:creator: Danni Guo, Hansong Huang, Shan Li, Xianfeng Zhao

item.title: Functions of $\boldsymbol{S}_p$-almost commuting unitary operators and contractions. An extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.01149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study functions of pairs of unitary operators and pairs of contractions with commutators in the Schatten-von Neumann class $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. We obtain commutator estimates and prove that our functional calculus is multiplicative modulo $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. On the other hand, we show that our commutator estimates do not extend to the case $p>2$. We also obtain an extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula. The main tool of this paper is a technique of triple operator integrals.
item.dc:creator: A. B. Aleksandrov, V. V. Peller

item.title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. III
item.description: arXiv:2611.01242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is the third in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices of size $n\times k$ with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough. In this part we study the remaining case where $k = 3$ and $n \ge k + 2 = 5$ and prove that every linear map preserving the Cullis' determinant admits the same description as for the case where $k \ge 4$ and $n \ge k + 2$ obtained previously.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Guterman, Andrey Yurkov

item.title: Counterexamples to uniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform under quadratic decay
item.description: arXiv:2611.01294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show nonuniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform on $\mathbb Z^2$ under quadratic decay. We construct an explicit nonzero function in $\ell^1(\mathbb Z^2)$ with pointwise decay $O(|z|^{-2})$ whose sums over integer lines vanish. We also obtain an infinite-dimensional null space with the same decay assumption. Furthermore, we show a result which indicates that the decay rate $|z|^{-2}$ may be sharp and faster decay may imply uniqueness.
item.dc:creator: Shubham R. Jathar, Jesse Railo

item.title: Similarity cancellation and primitive operator roots
item.description: arXiv:2611.01298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kaplansky's second test problem for similarity asks whether $A\oplus A\sim B\oplus B$ implies $A\sim B$ for bounded operators on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. We answer this question in the negative, even for compact operators whose singular values satisfy any prescribed positive upper bounds tending to zero. We also show that cancellation can fail under the stronger hypothesis $J_2(T)\sim J_2(S)$ considered by Marcoux, Radjavi, Troscheit, and Zhang \cite{MRTZ}. For these operators, finite amplifications and primitive roots are similar exactly at even multiplicities and even orders, respectively. In contrast, cancellation in fixed matrix size admits a uniform bound on the condition number. This extends the finite type~$I$ results of Jiang, Ma, Shi, and Zhang \cite{JMSZ}. The bound also holds for simultaneous similarity of arbitrary families of matrices and can be chosen to tend to one as the amplified bound tends to one. We conclude that, in a finite type~$I$ von Neumann algebra, cancellation of doubles and cancellation of primitive square roots are each equivalent to boundedness of the orders of its nonzero homogeneous summands.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Amine Aouichaoui

item.title: Optimal lengths of commutators of idempotents and similarity of nilpotent operators to their negatives
item.description: arXiv:2611.01316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\HH$ be a complex separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. We prove that every operator in $\BH$ is a sum of three commutators of idempotents and a product of two such commutators. Both numbers are best possible. The same is true for differences of idempotents, for operators similar to their negatives, and for operators anticommuting with an involution. Each of these four classes therefore has additive length three and multiplicative length two. We also construct nilpotent operators of order three that are similar to their negatives but cannot be conjugated to their negatives by any bounded involution. These results answer Question~7.22(a)--(c), the question in Remark~7.17, and the question about involutions in Section~2.9 of Marcoux, Radjavi and Zhang, \emph{J. Funct. Anal.} \textbf{284} (2023), 109854.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Amine Aouichaoui

item.title: A short proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality in dimension three
item.description: arXiv:2611.01416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a short proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality with sharp constant $2$ for matrices of dimension at most three.
item.dc:creator: Sam Looi

item.title: The ball fixed point property for continuous functions on locally compact spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and $p\in K$. We prove that the Banach space $C(K,p)=\{f\in C(K,\mathbb R):f(p)=0\}$ fails the ball fixed point property (BFPP) whenever $p$ is non-isolated, answering a question of Avil\'es, Jap\'on, Lennard, Mart\'inez-Cervantes and Stawski. Consequently, $C_0(L)$ fails the BFPP for every noncompact locally compact Hausdorff space $L$. Together with Barroso's characterization for $C(K)$, this yields complete topological classifications of the BFPP for $C_0(L)$ and $C(K,p)$. We also resolve a second question of Avil\'es et al., showing that the BFPP of $C(K)$ implies that of $C(K,p)$ for every compact Hausdorff space $K$ and every $P$-point $p\in K$ if and only if there are no measurable cardinals.
item.dc:creator: Lily DiPaulo

item.title: A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
item.description: arXiv:2611.01503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain a complete bound independent of the two disks, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.
item.dc:creator: Mihai Putinar, Georgios Tsikalas

item.title: Alternating chains and lattice strict singularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.01504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an alternating-chain argument intended to show that every lattice strictly singular operator from a real Banach lattice to a real Banach space is disjointly strictly singular. A hypothetical counterexample yields two LSS operators on a reflexive sequence lattice whose difference is bounded below. Quotienting by the range of that difference gives a common map bounded below on a positive tail cone. Finite chains of positive disjoint vectors, with alternating small differences, then lead to incompatible length estimates. We record the resulting operator and sequence consequences and extend the construction to common postcompositions with DSS errors. Independently of the proposed equality, we prove simultaneous nuclear restriction results for countable DSS families and uniform nuclear tails for norm-compact DSS families, together with common Hilbert-space factors and arbitrarily small nuclear corrections having a common infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples identify limits of these selection statements. The main equality is a candidate real-field proof; no complex-field equality is asserted.
item.dc:creator: Ma Yicen

item.title: Transfer of similarity to Hilbert space contractions through inner functions: a proof of Douglas's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.01703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A$ be a bounded operator on a Hilbert space and let $u$ be a non-constant Blaschke product, finite or infinite. We prove that if the spectrum of $A$ does not meet the closure of the set of poles of $u$, then $u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is. This settles a conjecture of R.G. Douglas. For infinite products $u$, no additional condition on the zeros beyond the Blaschke condition is required. We also show that '$u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is' for all non-constant inner functions $u$ whose reflected singularity set, the closure of the set of poles together with the singular support, avoids the spectrum of $A$. We also prove a weighted resolvent version of the theorem, which allows the poles to accumulate on the spectrum to a limited extent; a column criterion for partial products, which is shown to force their norm convergence; and a simultaneous version for commuting tuples of operators tested by separated inner functions sharing one Lyapunov operator. For finite Blaschke products we obtain a polynomial form of the Lyapunov operator, which gives an estimate for the similarity constants. We also characterise the tuples of finite Blaschke products that form a uniform strong test collection: they are exactly the tuples that are injective, with non-vanishing joint derivative, on the closed disc. Finally, we show by examples that the separation hypothesis cannot be replaced by the existence of a bounded $H^\infty$ calculus, by the existence of a norm radial limit, or by the strong convergence of the partial products, even for Ritt operators.
item.dc:creator: Catalin Badea

item.title: Algebraic properties of Toeplitz operators on annulus and multiply connected domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.01717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space over the annulus and provide a complete characterization of them. Based on that, we single out a certain class of Toeplitz operators that satisfy the multiplicativity property and lead to a zero product theorem. We further extend the results for the general multiply-connected domain and prove the zero product theorem for Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space over such a domain.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Adhikari, Susmita Das

item.title: Improved Berezin--Li--Yau Bounds for Dirichlet Eigenvalues via Fourier Coupling and Frequency Concentration
item.description: arXiv:2611.01741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $0<\lambda_1\leq\lambda_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of an open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$. We develop two Fourier-space refinements of the Berezin--Li--Yau argument. For every finite-measure open set, coordinate commutator identities and coupled scalar--vector projections lead to a one-dimensional variational constant $C_n^{\mathrm{new}}$ and the individual bound \[ \lambda_k\geq C_n^{\mathrm{new}}(2\pi)^2\omega_n^{-2/n} |\Omega|^{-2/n}k^{2/n}, \qquad \frac{n}{n+2}<c_n^{\mathrm{env}}<C_n^{\mathrm{new}}<1. \] Here $n/(n+2)$ is the classical Li--Yau individual coefficient and $c_n^{\mathrm{env}}$ is the coefficient associated with the uncoupled scalar envelope developed in our previous paper. Thus the displayed strict hierarchy separates the gain of the scalar energy envelope from the further gain supplied by the commutator coupling. For bounded open sets, a frequency-concentration operator, its first two traces, and the Ky Fan principle force Fourier mass outside the Li--Yau filling ball. A two-region bathtub argument then gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j \geq \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega) \frac{n}{n+2}(2\pi)^2\omega_n^{-2/n} |\Omega|^{-2/n}k^{1+2/n}, \qquad \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega)>1, \] where $\mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega)$ is strictly decreasing in $k$ and converges to one, and \[ \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega)-1\geq \frac{n+2}{2(n+1)^2} \left(\frac{\omega_{n-1}}{\omega_n}\right)^2 \left(\frac34\right)^{n-1}k^{-2/n}. \] Thus the sharp leading term in the Berezin--Li--Yau sum is supplemented by an explicit positive, volume-only correction of order $k$. Apart from boundedness in the concentration argument, no boundary regularity, convexity, or connectedness is assumed. These improvements do not prove P\'{o}lya's conjecture: the individual coefficient is below one, and the sum multiplier tends to one.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Wang, Hehu Xie

item.title: Carleson Measures and Integral Operators on Fock--Sobolev Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For integers $n\ge1$ and $N\ge0$, let $\mathbf g=(g_0,\ldots,g_N)$ be a vector of entire functions. We consider the generalized integral operator \ [T_{\mathbf g}^{(n,N)}f =I^n\!\left(\sum_{j=0}^N g_jf^{(j)}\right), \qquad (Ih)(z)=\int_0^z h(w)\dd w. \] We characterize its boundedness and compactness between Fock--Sobolev spaces $\F_m^p$ and $\F_\ell^q$, where $0<p,q<\infty$ and $m,\ell\ge0$ are integers. The coefficients of critical total degree determine the operator modulo compact operators and yield essential-norm estimates. In the Hilbert case, a Laurent Toeplitz representation gives the exact essential norm, a Fredholm criterion and an index formula. As an application, we obtain conditions for solutions of linear differential equations to belong to Fock--Sobolev spaces, including a necessary and sufficient polynomial zero condition in the Hilbert case. For entire functions $u_0,\ldots,u_N$ and $\varphi$, we also characterize boundedness, compactness and essential norms of the operators \[ L_{\mathbf u,\varphi}^{(N)}f =\sum_{j=0}^N u_j\,f^{(j)}\circ\varphi. \] The proofs use Carleson measure characterizations for finite sums of weighted differentiation operators on Fock--Sobolev spaces.
item.dc:creator: Jianxiang Dong, Shibo Hu

item.title: Tensor Products and the Isomorphic Theory of Daugavet Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.02060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct two separable Banach spaces with the Daugavet property whose injective and projective tensor squares, respectively, fail the Daugavet property. Both examples arise from one sequence of finite-dimensional extensions. The first space is the completion of the increasing union of the extensions, whereas the second is the closed span of their coordinate functionals. We will also investigate the operator Daugavet properties of these spaces later in the paper, also highlighting natural examples of metric spaces \(M\) for which \(\operatorname{Lip}_0(M)\) has the Daugavet property but fails to have the weak operator Daugavet property. Independently of this, we will also prove that every Banach space admits a linear isometric embedding into a Banach space which is not isomorphic to any Banach space with the Daugavet property.
item.dc:creator: Samir Hamad

item.title: Sobolev spaces arising from the Stockwell transform on Gelfand pairs
item.description: arXiv:2611.02175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a family of Sobolev-type spaces on Gelfand pairs, built from the Stockwell transform: a function belongs to the space of a given smoothness when its Stockwell transform, multiplied by a weight that grows with the smoothness, is square integrable. We prove that these spaces are Hilbert spaces, that they form a decreasing scale under continuous embeddings, and that an interpolation inequality controls the norm at an intermediate smoothness by the norms at the two endpoints. Under integrability conditions on the weight and on the family of analysing windows, they embed continuously into Lebesgue spaces. Under a local domination condition on the window, we show that their elements have bounded continuous representatives. On the Euclidean motion group, where the Stockwell transform reduces to a windowed Hankel transform, this gives boundedness and continuity as soon as the smoothness exceeds half the dimension, which is the classical threshold for Euclidean spaces.
item.dc:creator: Claude G. Dosseh, Mawoussi Todjro, Yaogan Mensah

item.title: Hardy transitions on product lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.02206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Boundary conditions can change the dimensional scale of a sharp functional inequality. We determine this change for inverse-square Hardy inequalities on the product lattices $\mathbb N^k\times\mathbb Z^{N-k}$. Their sharp constants satisfy $C_{N,k}\sim N^2\Psi(k/N)$ uniformly for $1\le k\le N$, where $\Psi(\alpha)\sim2\alpha$ at zero. The law gives linear growth for a fixed number of positive coordinates, every intermediate power for suitable sublinear choices, and quadratic growth for a positive proportion. We develop a method that connects exact uncertainty inequalities with Hardy inequalities through logarithmic localization, and combines this transfer with a block decomposition to cover all proportions. The transfer holds on weighted graphs with an explicit geometric error and controls the variational problem over arbitrary functions. A mixture of two Mathieu ground energies determines $\Psi$. At the fully positive endpoint, the variational problem defining $\kappa=\Psi(1)$ has a unique nondegenerate minimum and a unique positive energy--moment minimizing profile. We also prove strict comparison with the continuum coefficient in every sector for $N\ge9$, the optimal uniform dimension.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Lizama

item.title: Jensen--Mercer-type Inequalities and Strongly $f$-Divergences
item.description: arXiv:2611.02518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop refined Jensen--Mercer-type inequalities for strongly convex functions, including reverse inequalities in the differentiable case. We identify the relationships between these inequalities and known bounds. Our method exploits a structural decomposition of strongly convex functions together with classical convexity arguments. As applications, we obtain explicit and computable bounds for strongly $f$-divergences, leading to new quantitative estimates for major divergence measures such as the Kullback--Leibler divergence, $\chi^{2}$-divergence, Hellinger divergence, Bhattacharyya-type divergence, and Jeffreys divergence.
item.dc:creator: Vidyanshu Kumar Rai, Ravinder Kumar

item.title: Sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities for solvable and semisimple Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.02597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we obtain the sharp constants for Hausdorff--Young inequalities on simply connected, completely solvable Lie groups, and connected real semisimple Lie groups with finite center.
item.dc:creator: Jinsong Wu, Fulin Yang

item.title: Extension of kappa-additive measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.02729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an extension theorem for kappa-additive probability measures, where kappa is an arbitrary uncountable cardinal. Starting from a <kappa-algebra, we define an outer measure using coverings of cardinality at most kappa and characterise measurable sets by approximation in outer measure of symmetric differences. We prove that these sets form a kappa-algebra carrying a complete kappa-additive extension of the original measure. The extension is unique on the generated kappa-algebra, and its completion is the minimal domain admitting a complete kappa-additive extension. We also establish attainment of the covering infimum and show why the closure assumption on the initial algebra is essential. Examples include a strict extension of classical Lebesgue measure under the additional hypothesis add N = aleph_1 < cov N.
item.dc:creator: Sviatoslav V. Dzhenzher

item.title: Operator Fej\'{e}r--Riesz Theorems with Gaps and Degree Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2611.02967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. We prove that every hermitian polynomial with bounded-operator coefficients that is positive semidefinite on $K$ belongs to the operator quadratic module generated by $S$. We also show that if such a polynomial has degree at most $\tt{d}$, then it admits a certificate of weighted degree at most $\tt{d}+c_S$, where $c_S$ depends only on $S$, not on the polynomial or the coefficient Hilbert space. In contrast to the scalar case, where natural preorderings admit the degree bound $\tt{d}$ independently of $K$, we show that no uniform additive constant exists for natural matrix preorderings. We construct quadratic $2\times2$ matrix polynomials positive semidefinite on unions of two intervals whose minimum certificate degrees in the corresponding natural preorderings diverge as one interval shrinks to a point, while the gap length remains bounded below. Conversely, we establish uniform bounds of the form $\tt{d}+C$ for families of interval unions contained in a fixed compact interval when interval lengths and gap lengths have uniform positive lower bounds. Our proofs develop two techniques that may be of independent interest. First, a quadratic reduction principle represents arbitrary-degree operator polynomials as compressions of quadratic ones on enlarged Hilbert spaces. A perturbation argument and the closedness of truncated operator quadratic modules then extend uniform degree bounds from the quadratic case to arbitrary degrees with linear degree bounds of slope $1$. Second, a rank-one symmetric matrix pencil transfers positivity on interval unions to $[0,1]$, where the operator Fej\'er--Riesz theorem yields certificates.
item.dc:creator: Abhay Jindal, Alja\v{z} Zalar

item.title: Joint Moments of Bilinear Resolvents
item.description: arXiv:2611.03081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given $A,B\in B\left(H\right)_{+}$, we consider the existence and uniqueness of a positive operator $C\in B\left(H\right)_{+}$ such that \[ \left(I+mA+nB+mnC\right)^{-1}=\int_{\left[0,1\right]^{2}}s^{m}t^{n}dE\left(s,t\right),\quad m,n\geq0, \] for a positive operator-valued measure $E$. This is a joint Hausdorff moment problem. Without $C$, it holds if and only if $AB=BA$. In dimension two we give a complete criterion for noncommuting pairs. In higher finite dimensions, nonexistence is generic. Under certain spectral and cyclicity assumptions, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition on arbitrary Hilbert spaces. The completion is unique in this case. We also classify these pairs up to unitary equivalence. The class includes irreducible infinite-dimensional examples, even with continuous spectrum.
item.dc:creator: James Tian

item.title: Unique Hahn-Banach extensions in Bochner $L^p$ spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.03203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Y$ be a closed subspace of a real Banach space $X$. Let $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a complete finite measure space and let $1<p<\infty$. We prove that $Y$ has property-$(U)$, property-$(SU)$, property-$(wU)$ in $X$ if and only if $L^p(\mu,Y)$ has the corresponding property in $L^p(\mu,X)$. No Radon-Nikod\'{y}m assumption on $X^*$ is required. The proofs use $w^*$-measurable representations of dual functionals and a simultaneous scalar-lifting construction. A norm-minimal representation for an element in $L^p(\mu,X)^*$ is found suitable in this case. We also study the point of continuity of the identity map under different topologies on the unit sphere of $L^p(\mu,X)^*$. For Bochner-integrable functionals, the pointwise $w^*-w$-continuity yields the uniqueness of the extension to $L^p(\mu,X^{**})$. Examples show why arbitrary $w^*$-measurable representatives cannot replace the norm-minimal representatives in this context.
item.dc:creator: Sainik Karak, Tanmoy Paul

item.title: A Stieltjes representation of order $p$ for $ \mathrm{tr}[(A+tB)^{-p}]$: Hein\"avaara's measure, B-splines, and Stahl's theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.03208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $A$ positive definite, $B$ positive semidefinite and $p\ge1$ we show that $\mathrm{tr}[(A+tB)^{-p}]=\int(1+t\ell)^{-p}\,d\rho_p(\ell)$ for a positive measure $\rho_p$ on the spectral interval of $L=A^{-1/2}BA^{-1/2}$, and we identify the measure: it has atoms $\mathrm{tr}[(P_sA^{-1}P_s)^p]$ at the eigenvalues of $L$ and a continuous density, an integral of Hein\"avaara's tracial joint spectral measure along rays. For integer $p$ the positivity of $\rho_p$ follows from the positivity of Hein\"avaara's measure alone, and the density is a sum of Curry-Schoenberg B-splines; for real $p$ the representation is obtained by inverting Hein\"avaara's transform. For $0<p<1$ the function is a Stieltjes function of order $p$ only if $[A,B]=0$, but a positive representation of order one holds, with an explicit density. Along $A_p=pI+A_0$, $p\to\infty$, the measures converge to the measure of Stahl's theorem (the Bessis-Moussa-Villani conjecture) for $\mathrm{tr}\,e^{-(A_0+tB)}$.
item.dc:creator: Luc Rey-Bellet

item.title: Lower bounds for Riesz interaction functionals
item.description: arXiv:2611.03215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the pressure formation problem for hydrodynamic models with nonlocal interactions, we classify strong Lebesgue lower bounds for the Riesz energy functional and for a determinant functional arising from the theory of compensated integrability. The classification covers all integrability exponents in $(0,\infty]$ within the class of confined log-concave densities. These geometric assumptions are motivated by counterexamples for general densities. On the whole space, neither functional controls any fixed Lebesgue quasi-norm. Under confinement, lower bounds fail for exponents greater than one, whereas $L^1$ bounds hold for the energy in every dimension and for the determinant only in dimension one. The log-concave estimates hold at sharp integrability exponents and follow from endpoint Lorentz bounds for confined quasiconcave densities and a weak-to-strong lemma. In particular, the energy estimates provide a geometric lower-bound counterpart to the classical Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality.
item.dc:creator: Nuno J. Alves, Athanasios E. Tzavaras

item.title: A height transportation approach to the quantitative Pr\'ekopa--Leindler inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.03295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a new, simpler proof of sharp stability for the Pr\'ekopa--Leindler inequality. In contrast to the main arguments from Figalli, van Hintum and Tiba~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}, our proof hinges mostly on the sharp stability theory for the Brunn--Minkowski problem, developed by the same authors \cite{figalli2024BM}, and on the idea of using a height transportation approach in order to match level sets. As a by-product of our techniques, we are able to prove the sharp dependency on $\tau = \min\{\lambda,1-\lambda\}$ in the Pr\'ekopa--Leindler stability constant whenever one of the inputs is logarithmically concave, producing a new, simplified proof of two of the main results from~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}. Finally, in the same fashion as Krist\'aly and P\^irvuceanu \cite{kristaly2026quantitative}, we are able to obtain new stability results for the Bakry-Emery log-Sobolev inequality and for the Talagrand inequality. Due to the sharpness of the inputs, these results are optimal in terms of exponents. We moreover show that the $L^1$ nature of the distance in such results \emph{cannot} in general be improved to any other $L^p$ distance, where $p>1.$
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Miguel Machado, Jo\~ao P. G. Ramos

item.title: A counterexample concerning weighted convolution on the integers
item.description: arXiv:2611.03334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $1<p<\infty$ and let $w:\mathbb{Z}\to(0,\infty)$ be a weight. When is the weighted space $\ell^p(\mathbb{Z},w)$ an algebra with respect to convolution? A well-known sufficient condition is that $(w^{-q}*w^{-q})/w^{-q}$ be bounded on $\mathbb{Z}$, where $q:=p/(p-1)$ is the index conjugate to $p$. We present an example to show that this sufficient condition is not necessary.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Morneau-Gu\'erin, Thomas Ransford

item.title: Frame Properties of Effective Stationary Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2611.03358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Kaczmarz algorithm is an iterative projection method for reconstructing vectors in a Hilbert space from inner product data. However, sequences that are effective for this algorithm need not be frames and may lack standard frame reconstruction properties. We investigate these properties for stationary effective sequences, which were classified by Kwapie\'n and Mycielski according to their spectral measures. In particular, we show that the corresponding Kaczmarz reconstruction series always converge unconditionally if and only if the spectral measure is atomic with finitely many point masses. We show that if the spectral measure is atomic, the stationary effective sequence and its auxiliary Parseval frame can be interchanged in the Kaczmarz reconstruction formula. Finally, we construct two stationary effective sequences with singular continuous spectral measures, one of which can be interchanged with its auxiliary Parseval frame in the reconstruction formula, and one of which cannot be interchanged.
item.dc:creator: Chad Berner, John E. Herr, Palle E. T. Jorgensen

item.title: Spectra of Beurling algebras of abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.03437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a complete classification of all sets which are spectra of Beurling algebras of any locally compact abelian group, parametrizing them by compact convex sets in the dual of a certain locally convex vector space generated by the group. Hence, for example, a finitely generated free abelian group may enjoy a more complicated range of such spectra than the does rational numbers.
item.dc:creator: Nico Spronk, Zhihao Zhang

item.title: Invariant mean on weakly almost periodic functionals over a Hopf-von Neumann algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.00431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let \(M\) be a Hopf--von Neumann algebra with predual \(M_*\). Using minimal weak*-closed left ideals, we obtain an idempotent state \(\varphi\in\operatorname{WAP}(M_*)^*\) satisfying \(\varphi\star \omega\star\varphi=\varphi\) for every state \(\omega\) on \(\operatorname{WAP}(M_*)\). This state determines the largest closed introverted subspace \(X_\varphi\subseteq\operatorname{WAP}(M_*)\) containing the identity and admitting a two-sided invariant mean. We also characterize the existence of a unique two-sided invariant mean on introverted operator systems in \(\operatorname{WAP}(M_*)\) by a symmetry condition on their left and right state orbits. The criterion recovers the classical results for locally compact groups and their Fourier algebras, and gives a unified treatment of cocommutative Hopf--von Neumann algebras, compact quantum groups, unital \(C^*\)-Eberlein algebras, and \(\operatorname{WAP}(M(G))\) for every locally compact group \(G\).
item.dc:creator: Ramin Faal, Hamid Reza Ebrahimi Vishki, Amin Allah Khosravi

item.title: The e-Property for Quantum Markov Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.00703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(\mathcal T_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let $\mathcal A$ be an invariant Feller $C^*$-algebra. We formulate the $e$-property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Ces\`aro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations. When every observable has the $e$-property, the Jacobs--de Leeuw--Glicksberg decomposition identifies the reversible Choi--Effros algebra and the norm-stable sector. Expected and decoherence-free subalgebras transfer the property under norm decay of the complementary dynamics, including infinite-dimensional ultracontractive and finite-index Pimsner--Popa regimes. Finally, we establish the full comparison hierarchy among ordinary, eventual, Ces\`aro and pointwise eventual equicontinuity notions, reinforced by matrix Jamison and homoclinic flow counterexamples. Projection-face criteria are treated in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kania, Mariusz Niwi\'nski

item.title: Spectral Theory and Continuum Norm Resolvent Convergence of a One-Sided Discrete Dirac-Type Operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.00820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate a one-dimensional discrete Dirac-type operator $D_d$ acting on the Hilbert space $\big(\ell^2(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$, obtained from the classical continuous free Dirac operator by replacing the spatial derivative with the one-sided backward difference operator $I - S_1$, where $S_1$ denotes the right shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})$. We establish the fundamental operator-theoretic and spectral properties of $D_d$: unlike symmetric or supersymmetric lattice discretizations, $D_d$ is bounded and non-normal for every non-zero rest mass $m > 0$, with self-commutator $[D_d, D_d^\dag] = -2mc^3(-\Delta_{\mathrm{disc}})\sigma_2$, yet it is quadratically normal. We compute the exact operator norm, determine the exact spectral radius in two mass regimes, and show via Fourier--Laurent analysis that the spectrum $\sigma(D_d)$ is purely continuous and lies on a two-component algebraic curve in the complex plane undergoing a topological transition at $mc^2 = 2c$. Finally, introducing a lattice spacing $h > 0$ and embedding $\big(\ell^2(h\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$ isometrically into $\big(L^2(\mathbb{R};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$ via Whittaker--Shannon band-limited interpolation, we prove that the scaled non-normal discrete Dirac-type operator $D_{d,h}$ converges to the continuous self-adjoint Dirac operator $D$ in the norm resolvent sense at the optimal rate $\mathcal{O}(h)$ as $h \to 0^+$, without requiring frequency cutoffs.
item.dc:creator: Mariusz Niwi\'nski

item.title: Continuous, locally Lipschitz and Lipschitz selections for intuitionistic fuzzy sets, with applications to expert voting
item.description:
arXiv:2611.00857v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies continuous selections in the framework of intuitionistic fuzzy sets. To each intuitionistic fuzzy set $A=(\mu,
u)$ on a topological space $X$ we associate the interval-valued map $F_{A}(x)=[\mu(x),1-
u(x)]$, whose width is the hesitation degree. Hence, in this setting, a selection of $F_{A}$ is an ordinary fuzzy membership function compatible with the intuitionistic information, and every selection is the membership function of Atanassov's operator $D_{\vartheta}$ for a suitable pointwise parameter $\vartheta$. When $X$ is normal and $\mu$, $
u$ are upper semi-continuous, a continuous selection exists by the Kat\v{e}tov--Tong insertion theorem. We show that upper semi-continuity arises naturally in a voting model, in which a panel of experts divides a metric universe into closed regions of acceptance and rejection, and for this model we construct an explicit continuous selection, the consensus selection, illustrated by a non-compact example in the plane. On metric spaces we characterise the intuitionistic fuzzy sets that admit an $L$-Lipschitz selection through a non-local version of the condition $\mu+
u\leq 1$, and we give the largest and the smallest such selections in closed form. Finally, we prove that the set of continuous selections depends in a $1$-Lipschitz way on the intuitionistic fuzzy set, with respect to the Hausdorff-type distance of Grzegorzewski. We also characterise the intuitionistic fuzzy sets admitting locally Lipschitz selections.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Failla, Gianmarco La Rosa, Marco Elio Tabacchi

item.title: Convergence of non-symmetric forms with changing reference measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.00975v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a functional-analytic theory of convergence for non-symmetric generalized Dirichlet forms defined on a sequence of Hilbert spaces $H_n$ converging to a limit space $H$ in the sense of Kuwae-Shioya, with the principal applications concerning $L^2$-spaces over varying reference measures $\mu_n \to \mu$. Extending Mosco's variational convergence for Dirichlet forms to the non-symmetric setting via a functional controlling the off diagonal values of the forms, we introduce a notion of generalized convergence of non-symmetric Dirichlet forms and show it to be equivalent to strong convergence of the associated resolvents, to weak convergence of the co-resolvents, and to strong graph convergence of the infinitesimal generators. A version of the Trotter-Kato theorem in the Kuwae-Shioya framework yields the corresponding equivalence for $C_0$-contraction semigroups. As applications, we give sufficient conditions for the generalized convergence of elliptic and sectorial $a_{i,j}$-forms with changing speed measures, both on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and in infinite dimensions over a Gelfand triple, and deduce weak convergence of the laws of the associated right processes under tightness of the path measures.
item.dc:creator: Jonas M. T\"olle

item.title: The sharp Stein-Tomas inequality on the circle
item.description: arXiv:2611.01318v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that constant functions are global maximizers for the endpoint Stein--Tomas inequality on $\mathbb{S}^1$, thereby determining its sharp constant. By the known characterization of the phases of maximizers, every nonzero maximizer then has the form $f(\omega)=c e^{ix_0\cdot\omega}$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Yaojun Wang

item.title: Stochastic Euler Products in the Paley-Wiener Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.01347v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: General sufficient conditions, in terms of stochastic Euler products, are given for a realization of a point process to have finite excess or finite deficiency in the Paley-Wiener space.
item.dc:creator: Alexander I. Bufetov

item.title: Decay of Correlations for Multiplicative Functionals of Determinantal Point Processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01379v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The main result of this paper is an upper bound on the correlations of multiplicative functionals of determinantal point processes. In particular, for the sine process, the correlations of a multiplicative functional associated with a rapidly decaying function decay quadratically. It follows that the spectral density of such functionals belongs to the Sobolev space $H_1$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander I. Bufetov

item.title: The Marvelous Meixner Polynomials: Second Kind, First Class
item.description: arXiv:2611.01422v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Meixner's classification asks which exponential generating functions can generate orthogonal polynomials. We follow the continuous Meixner family from this question to its moments, measures, and continued fractions. A beta integral and a bilinear identity establish positivity and orthogonality; Carlitz's Bernoulli and Euler constructions reveal further connections. Turning the parameter into a variable leads to rational orthogonality and Wall's fraction. We derive its Nevanlinna measure and unite the two spectral directions in a joint law with Cauchy marginals. Even finite pencils produce couplings with these exact marginals. Laguerre limits explain the gamma law governing joint extremes. Along the way, Meixner's scientific life, combinatorics, tangent numbers, and even zeta values illuminate the same structure.
item.dc:creator: Olga Holtz

item.title: Half-space polynuclear growth: KPZ universality
item.description: arXiv:2611.01475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study polynuclear growth (PNG) on the half-line with Poisson nucleations in the bulk and at the boundary. For every nonnegative boundary nucleation rate, we construct stationary measures and jointly stationary couplings under a common graphical environment, with profiles pinned at the origin. We realize these couplings as a measurable stationary PNG horizon and prove convergence to the half-space stationary horizon under Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling. The horizon convergence includes its base profile and positive representing measure, together with joint profile convergence at every prescribed finite parameter list. We also prove convergence of the height evolution from general upper-semicontinuous initial profiles to the half-space KPZ fixed point. The associated passage field converges locally uniformly to the half-space directed landscape, jointly with evolutions from finitely many initial profiles driven by the same environment. The convergence results cover the critical boundary window and every fixed subcritical boundary rate, including zero. All fixed subcritical rates produce the same limiting laws.
item.dc:creator: Kailun Chen

item.title: Bound states at Trudinger--Moser growth: obstructions, pairing and bubbling
item.description: arXiv:2611.01575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study radial solutions of the planar scalar field equation $$ -\Delta u+u=\lambda u\,e^{u^2}, \qquad 0<\lambda<1, $$ whose nonlinearity has critical Trudinger--Moser growth. These solutions describe standing waves of the two-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"odinger and Klein--Gordon equations. Motivated by Tang's recent uniqueness result for radial bound states with power nonlinearities in higher dimensions, we investigate the validity of the corresponding uniqueness theory at critical exponential growth. We show that the Serrin--Tang criterion and two structural hypotheses in Tang's analysis fail in this setting. We establish a pairing principle for the shooting problem, prove that Tang's variation conditions force the nodal count to be non-decreasing, and show that any two radial ground states intersect. We also derive a second-order expansion of the Liouville bubble arising at large initial heights and compute the corresponding flux correction. These asymptotics yield formal predictions for the first zero and the nodal structure at large heights. Our results suggest that the ground state is unique, whereas nodal radial bound states, if they exist, occur in pairs, contrary to the uniqueness phenomenon for power nonlinearities.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Majdoub

item.title: A Banach--Stone-like Theorem for Slowly Oscillating Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every lattice isomorphism between the lattices of slowly oscillating real-valued functions on proper metric spaces induces a coarse homeomorphism. This yields a Banach--Stone-like theorem for slowly oscillating functions, as well as a representation theorem for linear lattice isomorphisms between these function lattices. Both theorems were previously established by the author under the assumption of chain-connectedness. The present paper establishes both results for arbitrary proper metric spaces.
item.dc:creator: Yutaka Iwamoto

item.title: An affine reverse Faber-Krahn inequality via information decay
item.description: arXiv:2611.02279v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ admits $S\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ such that $\lambda_1(SK)|K|^{2/n}\le Cn$, where $C$ is universal. For origin-symmetric bodies of volume one, the bound holds in maximal Gaussian measure position. The main step is the spectral estimate \[ \lambda_1(D)\le C(P)\bigl(n+\sqrt{n I(\nu\mid\gamma_n)}\bigr) \] for an even isotropic log-concave probability measure $\nu$ supported on a symmetric convex body $D$, with Poincar\'e constant at most $P$ and finite relative Fisher information. A second-order Stein estimate and an information jump under convolution give entropy decay faster than $m^{-1}$ for normalised sums. Their supports control the Gaussian measure of dilates, and a Brownian bridge expansion gives the spectral estimate. A Gaussian-weighted ground state supplies a measure whose Fisher information is bounded in terms of $\lambda_1(K)$. The square-root dependence then gives the bound of order $n$.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Colbrook, George Stepaniants

item.title: On the dichotomy of $p$-walk dimensions on metric measure spaces II
item.description: arXiv:2611.02422v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On a volume doubling metric measure space endowed with a family of $p$-energies such that the Poincar\'e inequality and the capacity upper bound with $p$-walk dimension $\beta_p$ hold, for $p$ in an open interval $I\subseteq(1,+\infty)$, we prove the following dichotomy: either $\beta_p=p$ for all $p\in I$, or the function $p\mapsto \frac{\beta_p}{p}$ takes values in $(1,+\infty)$ and is strictly decreasing on $I$. Moreover, if the metric measure space is $d_h$-Ahlfors regular, we prove the following dichotomy: either $\beta_p=d_h+p-1$ for all $p\in I$, or the function $p\mapsto \frac{\beta_p-d_h}{p-1}$ takes values in $(-\infty,1)$ and is strictly increasing on $I$.
item.dc:creator: Meng Yang

item.title: Noncommutative extensions of an ergodic theorem of Breiman
item.description: arXiv:2611.02535v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra, $T:L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)\to L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ be induced by a normal $\tau$-preserving $*$-automorphism of $\mathcal{M}$, and $x\in L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)$. We will prove the bilaterally almost uniform convergence of averages of the form $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T^k(x_k),$$ generalizing an ergodic theorem proven by Breiman in \cite{Breiman57}, where $(x_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is an element of the noncommutative vector-valued $L_p$-space $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau;\ell_\infty)$ such that there exists $x\in L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ with $(x_k-x)_{k=0}^{\infty}\in L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau;c_0)$. A generalization to semifinite $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ and general positive Dunford-Schwartz operators $T\in DS^+(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ is shown as well when $1<p<\infty$. In addition to these, we also prove a number of generalizations of the results to weighted, subsequential, and other types of averages.
item.dc:creator: Morgan O'Brien

item.title: Planar Convexity of Isotropy Orbits via Cohomology and Common Zeros
item.description: arXiv:2611.02575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a noncompact simple real Lie algebra with a Cartan decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{k}\oplus\mathfrak{p}$. Let $K$ denote the connected Lie group corresponding to $\mathfrak{k}$. Then $K$ acts on $\mathfrak{p}$ via the adjoint representation. In this paper, we prove that for every $C\in\mathfrak{p}$ and every real linear map $L:\mathfrak{p}\to\mathbb{R}^2$, the linear image $L(K\cdot C)$ of the orbit $K\cdot C\subset\mathfrak{p}$ is convex in $\mathbb{R}^2$, except for the circle orbits when $\mathfrak{g}\cong\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $C\ne0$. By the two-piece property of isotropy orbits, any point omitted from the interior of the convex hull of a planar projection induces a nonzero class in the first integral cohomology of the orbit. This class vanishes directly in the non-Hermitian case, whereas in the Hermitian case we show that it vanishes by using the central circle action and a common-zero theorem of Gichev for Laplace eigenfunctions. Our approach treats classical and exceptional noncompact simple real Lie algebras uniformly and extends to real semisimple Lie algebras via Minkowski sums.
item.dc:creator: Yongzhi Luan, Tin-Yau Tam

item.title: Bilinear maximal functions associated with some degenerate surfaces on the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2611.02745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the works of Lee--Shuin and Borges--Foster on the Euclidean space, in this article we consider bilinear averages on the Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^n$ corresponding to some degenerate surfaces associated with the Kor\'anyi norm as well as Nevo--Thangavelu type averaging structures, and study the boundedness of the their full and lacunary maximal functions on various $L^{p}(\mathbb{H}^n) \times L^{q}(\mathbb{H}^n)$ spaces, for $n \geq 2$. For the full maximal functions, we obtain optimal range except possibly at the end points.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Bagchi, Rahul Garg, Surya Kanta Rana

item.title: Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
item.description: arXiv:2611.02886v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Auscher (LMO)

item.title: Corona and Gleason problems for certain Banach spaces of holomorphic functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.02949v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use a combination of the classical dead-end space method and the interpolation (by bounded holomorphic functions) method to affirmatively solve Corona and Gleason problems for familiar Banach spaces of holomorphic functions such as (Besov-)Lipschitz spaces of holomorphic functions on bounded symmetric domains (including the unit ball and polydisc) in $\mathbb{C}^n$, holomorphic mean (Besov-)Lipschitz spaces, (Besov-)Hardy-Sobolev spaces and some special classes of holomorphic mixed-norm (Bergman) spaces (including weighted Bergman spaces) as well as some special classes of holomorphic (mean) Besov-Lipschitz spaces on the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$. Indeed, we extend our recent work on both problems for holomorphic Lipschitz algebras.
item.dc:creator: S. R. Patel

item.title: High-order fractional linear differential equations do not describe stochastic processes with finite state space
item.description: arXiv:2611.02954v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The replacement of the classical derivative in the governing equation of a continuous-time Markov process with finite state space by a fractional derivative of arbitrary order $\alpha>1$ produces solutions that are mathematically incompatible with the theory of stochastic processes.
item.dc:creator: P. Van Mieghem

item.title: The kinetic Kato square root problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.03104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.
item.dc:creator: Kaj Nystr\"om

item.title: Rigidity of the Peres-Vir\'ag class
item.description: arXiv:2611.03118v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Consider the hyperbolic Gaussian analytic function (GAF) \begin{equation*} F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }\xi _{n}z^{n},\qquad |z|<1, \end{equation*} where the $\xi _{n}$ are independent standard complex Gaussian variables. Peres-Vir\'{a}g theorem tells that the distribution of the zeros of $F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)$ is provided by a Determinantal Point Process (DPP). We prove that $F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)$ is the only GAF whose zeros are determinantal with a Hermitian kernel, up to multiplication by a zero-free holomorphic function and a one-to-one holomorphic change of variable, with a \ non-degeneracy condition imposed to exclude trivial cases. The proof identifies a geometric property of GAF's with (local) determinantal zeros: the metric defined by the first intensity must have constant curvature $-4$.
item.dc:creator: Lu\'is Daniel Abreu

item.title: A Note on Fractional Sobolev inequalities revisited
item.description: arXiv:2611.03185v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we extend the analysis of homogeneous fractional Sobolev inequalities in the paper by A.D. Nguyen, J. I. D{\i}az, and Q.-H. Nguyen (2020). We combine their subcritical proof with the first author's adaptation to the supercritical case to provide a short interpolation-based proof for the critical case.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Leoni, Asher Wheaton

item.title: Near-optimal bounds for the critical 2d SHF and the delta-Bose gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.03191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a near-optimal upper bound $\exp(\exp(CN^{1+o(1)}))$ for the $N$-th moment of the critical two-dimensional stochastic heat flow, improving on the bound $\exp(\exp(CN^{2}))$ of Gu, Quastel, and Tsai. Near-optimality follows from the lower bound $\exp(\exp(cN))$ of Ganguly and Nam. These estimates establish the exponential scale of the ground-state energy of the two-dimensional $N$-body delta-Bose gas predicted by Rajeev's conjecture, up to a vanishing error in the exponent. As a further step toward this conjecture, we derive, for each fixed $N$, a formula for the ground-state energy in terms of the bottom of the spectrum of a principal operator.
item.dc:creator: Xue-Mei Li, Te-Chun Wang

item.title: Characterization of the group Fourier transform of Hilbert space Valued functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03267v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A remarkable theorem of S. Alesker, S. Artstein-Avidan, and V. Milman characterizes the Fourier transform on $\mathbb{R}^n$ as, in essence, the unique transformation on the space of tempered distributions that exchanges convolution with pointwise multiplication. In this paper, we extend this perspective to the setting of the Heisenberg group $\He$, focusing on functions taking values in a separable Hilbert space $\Hi$. We establish a characterization of the group Fourier transform on $\He$ in terms of convolution. More precisely, we characterize the group Fourier transform on $L^1(\He,\Hi)$ and $L^2(\He,\Hi)$. In addition, we obtain a similar characterization for the group Fourier transform of $\Hi$-valued Schwartz class functions on the Heisenberg group.
item.dc:creator: Satyajyoti Achar, Md Hasan Ali Biswas, Ramesh Manna

item.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.03527v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schr\"odinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.
item.dc:creator: Yinghao Gong

item.title: Counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture from the viewpoint of lineability
item.description: arXiv:2611.03572v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Algebraic genericity in the family of polynomial counterexamples to the recently solved Jacobian Conjecture for $N\ge3$ is investigated. The notion of affine-coneability is introduced and it is shown that this family is affine-coneable and 1-lineable, but not 2-lineable. Semigroupability is further studied with respect to coordinatewise multiplication and composition.
item.dc:creator: L. Bernal-Gonz\'alez, M. C. Calder\'on-Moreno, J. A. Prado-Bassas

item.title: Frechet differential of a power series in Banach algebras
item.description: arXiv:0804.2836v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present two new forms in which the Frechet differential of a power series in a Banach algebra can be expressed in terms of absolutely convergent series involving the commutant $C(T):A\mapsto [A,T]$.Then we apply the results to the analytic functional calculus in a complex Banach space.
item.dc:creator: Benedetto Silvestri

item.title: Integral equalities for functions of unbounded spectral operators in Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:0804.3069v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a limiting procedure for extending local integral operator equalities to the global ones and to applying it to obtaining generalizations of the Newton-Leibnitz formula for operator-valued maps for a wide class of unbounded operators.
item.dc:creator: Benedetto Silvestri

item.title: Use of bundles of locally convex spaces in problems of convergence of semigroups of operators defined on different Banach spaces. Applications to spectral stability problems
item.description: arXiv:0906.2953v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work we construct certain general bundles $<\mathfrak{M},\rho,X>$ and $<\mathfrak{B},\eta,X>$ of Hausdorff locally convex spaces associated with a given Banach bundle $<\mathfrak{E},\pi,X>$. Then we present conditions ensuring the existence of bounded sections $\mathcal{U}\in \Gamma^{x_{\infty}}(\rho)$ and $\mathcal{P}\in \Gamma^{x_{\infty}}(\eta)$ both continuous at a point $x_{\infty}\in X$, such that $\mathcal{U}(x)$ is a $C_{0}-$semigroup of contractions on $\mathfrak{E}_{x}$ and $\mathcal{P}(x)$ is a spectral projector of the infinitesimal generator of the semigroup $\mathcal{U}(x)$, for every $x\in X$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Eurasian Math. J. 7,3 (2016) 53-88; Eurasian Math. J. 7,4 (2016) 46-78; Eurasian Math. J. 8,3 (2017) 85-108
item.dc:creator: Benedetto Silvestri

item.title: Construction of a Natural Transformation from a Classical to a Quantum 0-Species
item.description: arXiv:1812.06548v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A natural transformation $\mathfrak{J}$ between functors valued in the category $\mathfrak{Chdv}_{0}$ is assembled. $\mathfrak{Chdv}_{0}$ is obtained by replacing both the categories $\mathrm{ptls}$ and $\mathrm{ptsa}$ with the category of topological linear spaces in the defining properties of the category $\mathfrak{Chdv}$ introduced in one of our previous papers. By letting a $\mathfrak{dp}$-valued functor be (classical) quantum whenever every its value is a dynamical pattern whose set map takes values in the set of (commutative) noncommutative topological unital $\ast-$algebras, and letting a (classical) quantum $0$-species be a $\mathfrak{Chdv}_{0}$-valued functor factorizing through the canonical functor from $\mathfrak{dp}$ to $\mathfrak{Chdv}_{0}$ into a (classical) quantum $\mathfrak{dp}$-valued functor, we have that the domain and codomain of $\mathfrak{J}$ are a classical and a quantum $0$-species respectively.
item.dc:creator: Benedetto Silvestri

item.title: Stokes-type Integral Equalities for Scalarly Essentially Integrable Locally Convex Vector Valued Forms which are Functions of an Unbounded Spectral Operator
item.description: arXiv:2010.02692v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work we establish a Stokes-type integral equality for scalarly essentially integrable forms on an orientable smooth manifold with values in the locally convex linear space $\langle B(G),\sigma(B(G),\mathcal{N})\rangle$, where $G$ is a complex Banach space and $\mathcal{N}$ is a suitable linear subspace of the norm dual of $B(G)$. This result widely extends the Newton-Leibnitz-type equality stated in one of our previous articles. To obtain our equality we generalize the main result of that article, and employ the Stokes theorem for smooth locally convex vector valued forms established in a prodromic paper. Two facts are remarkable. Firstly the forms integrated involved in the equality are functions of a possibly unbounded scalar type spectral operator in $G$. Secondly these forms need not be smooth nor even continuously differentiable.
item.dc:creator: Benedetto Silvestri

item.title: A nonstandard analysis approach to limit operators and Fredholmness in Roe-like algebras
item.description: arXiv:2412.08130v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(X,d)$ be a uniformly locally finite metric space, and $T$ an operator in the uniform Roe algebra $C_u^*(X)$ (or uniform quasi-local algebra $C_{ql}^*(X)$). In this paper, we introduce the concept of limit operators of $T$ on galaxies in the nonstandard extension of $X$, and prove that $T$ is a generalized Fredholm operator with respect to the ghost ideal in $C_u^*(X)$ (or $C_{ql}^*(X)$) if and only if all limit operators on afar galaxies are invertible, and their inverses are uniformly bounded. In particular, if $X$ has Yu's Property A, then $T$ is a Fredholm operator if and only if all limit operators on afar galaxies are invertible. Using techniques in nonstandard analysis, our result strengthens a work of \v{S}pakula--Willett \cite{SpW} on the characterization of Fredholmness by using less limit operators.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Guo, L., Qian, J. and Wang, Q. (2026), A nonstandard analysis approach to limit operators and Fredholmness in Roe-like algebras. Bull. London Math. Soc., 58: e70534
item.dc:creator: Liang Guo, Jin Qian, Qin Wang

item.title: Estimates for convolution operators on Hardy spaces associated with ball quasi-Banach function spaces
item.description: arXiv:2511.21642v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $0 \leq \alpha < n$, $N \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $X$ and $Y$ be ball quasi-Banach function spaces on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We consider operators $T_{\alpha}$ defined by convolution with kernels of type $(\alpha, N)$. Assuming that the powered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator satisfies a Fefferman-Stein vector-valued maximal inequality on $X$ and is bounded on the associated space, we prove that, for $\alpha = 0$, $T_0$ extends to a bounded operator $H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to X$ and $H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n)$; and for $0 < \alpha < n$, under certain additional assumptions on $X$ and $Y$, $T_{\alpha}$ extends to a bounded operator $H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to Y$ and $H_{X}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to H_{Y}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. In particular, these results yield the corresponding estimates for singular integral operators and Riesz potentials. We also provide an off-diagonal Fefferman-Stein vector-valued inequality for the fractional maximal operator on the $p$-convexification of ball quasi-Banach function spaces.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Rocha

item.title: Semiprojective Banach lattices
item.description: arXiv:2604.10624v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a norm-controlled notion of semiprojectivity for Banach lattices, testing sequential quotient towers in separable ambient lattices and requiring arbitrarily small norm loss at a fixed stage. For a locally compact second-countable Hausdorff space $X$, we prove that $C_0(X)$ is semiprojective if and only if $X$ is compact and an absolute neighbourhood retract. Finite $\ell_1$-sums preserve semiprojectivity, and arbitrary $\ell_1$-sums of $1^+$-projective lattices are semiprojective without any order-unit assumption. By contrast, $\mathbb{R} \oplus_\infty \ell_1$ fails to be semiprojective, showing that neither semiprojectivity nor $1^+$-projectivity is preserved by finite $\ell_\infty$-sums, extensions, or pullbacks over a projective base. Every separable semiprojective lattice is $\lambda$-projective for some finite $\lambda$, and its scalar-valued lattice homomorphisms separate points. Consequently, a separable reflexive Banach lattice is semiprojective precisely when it is finite-dimensional, and no nonzero separable atomless order-continuous lattice is semiprojective. We also characterise $\ell$-openness as $1^+$-projectivity relative to separable ambient lattices; for separable domains this is ordinary $1^+$-projectivity. The restriction to separable ambient lattices is redundant for separable domains but affects the nonseparable examples.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kania, Mariusz Niwi\'nski

item.title: Periodicity in Banach algebras
item.description: arXiv:2606.29525v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider operators that are compositions of an isometric isomorphism and a left multiplier on a Banach algebra, and we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for these operators to have a dense set of periodic elements. As an application of this result, we characterize generalized weighted shifts with a dense set of periodic elements on the standard Hilbert module over C*-algebra of compact operators on a separable Hilbert space. As another application, we characterize generalized weighted shifts with a dense set of periodic elements on the standard Hilbert module over commutative non-unital C*-algebra. Finally, in the last section of the paper, we provide extensions of these results from the case of a sequence generated by powers of a single operator to families of operators indexed over a countable set.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Ivkovic

item.title: Polish spaces of separable Banach lattices
item.description: arXiv:2607.08064v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compare two Polish presentations of separable real Banach lattices: closed sublattices of a universal lattice and closed ideals of $\operatorname{FBL}[\ell_1]$. We construct translations preserving lattice isometry in both directions, continuous and injective from sublattices to ideals and Borel in the reverse direction. Natural generation and Fremlin tensor operations are $\boldsymbol\Sigma^0_2$-measurable with $G_\delta$ graphs. Isometric lattice isomorphism in either universal coding is Borel bireducible with a complete orbit equivalence relation of Polish-group actions. Uniform monotonicity and order uniform smoothness are $\boldsymbol\Pi^0_3$-complete in both codings, whereas strict monotonicity, order smoothness, and order continuity are coanalytic. Abstract $L_p$ and AM-spaces form closed classes of sublattice codes. We also give explicit Borel bounds for atom counts, compact order intervals, and the lattice-isometry classes of $L_p[0,1]$, $\ell_p$, and $c_0$.
item.dc:creator: Mariusz Niwi\'nski

item.title: The first chiral homology group in higher genus
item.description: arXiv:2607.24719v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the theory of the first chiral homology group of vertex algebras, developed by van Ekeren and Heluani for elliptic curves, to compact Riemann surfaces of arbitrary genus. Our approach realizes a genus $g$ surface by iterated self-sewing of $g$ handles onto the Riemann sphere, each governed by a sewing parameter $\rho_i$ in a punctured disc. We construct an explicit complex computing the chiral homology groups $H^{\mathrm{ch}}_0$ and $H^{\mathrm{ch}}_1$ of a vertex algebra $V$ on a genus $g$ surface with $n$ marked points, and equip it with a projectively flat connection, with an explicit central-charge anomaly, over the $g$-dimensional space of sewing parameters. We prove a genus $g$ Fourier-space Borcherds identity for the associated modified vertex operators. We show that two finiteness assumptions 1) finite dimensionality of the first Poisson homology $\HP_1(R_V)$ of the Zhu $C_2$-algebra, and 2) finite generation of a certain Koszul homology of the associated graded algebra, imply finite dimensionality of $H^{\mathrm{ch}}_1(X,V)$ for every genus $g$ and every vertex algebra $V$. Using the degeneration $\rho_i \to 0$ together with the factorization theorem of Damiolini-Gibney-Tarasca, we relate the totally degenerate limit of $H_1^{\mathrm{ch}}$ to the Hochschild homology of an iterated construction on the Zhu algebra, and deduce vanishing of the first chiral homology group in every genus for rational vertex algebras.
item.dc:creator: A. Zuevsky

item.title: Pointwise function spaces over compacta are not weak Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.17549v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and let $E$ be an infinite-dimensional real Banach space. We prove that there is no continuous bijection $h\colon C_p(K)\to E_w$ whose inverse is continuous at $h(0)$. Consequently, $C_p(K)$ and $C_w(L)$ are not homeomorphic for any infinite compact Hausdorff spaces $K$ and $L$. This settles Krupski's problem and its two-space version due to Krupski and Marciszewski, and answers a question of K\k{a}kol, Leiderman, and Michalak concerning $C_p([0,1])$ and weak Banach spaces.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kania, Jerzy K\k{a}kol

item.title: Duality and Baire like properties in topological abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.14074v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article investigates the duality of abelian topological groups by delving into the interplay between the algebraic and topological properties of a group $G$ and those of its dual group. In particular, extending the notion of a $g$-barrelled group, we introduce and study the classes of $\kappa$-barrelled and $\omega$-barrelled groups. Our first main result establishes that every $\omega$-barrelled group is $\aleph_0$-barrelled (i.e., if every weakly convergent sequence in the dual group is equicontinuous, then every metrizable weakly compact subset of the dual group is also equicontinuous). From this, we deduce that the free topological abelian group $A(K)$ over a metrizable compact space $K$ is determined by the subgroup generated by any of its dense subsets. Furthermore, we prove that if $G$ is a $\sigma$-compact, $\omega$-barrelled group, then its dual group $\widehat{G}_\kappa$ equipped with the compact-open topology is sequentially complete (complete if $G$ is hemicompact). We also solve an open question posed by Trigos-Arrieta by constructing an explicit example of an $\omega$-barrelled metrizable group that fails to be $g$-barrelled. Finally, we investigate the dualization of groups lacking infinite compact subsets, proving that for a totally bounded abelian group $G$, every compact subset of $G$ is finite if and only if its dual group $\widehat{G}$, endowed with the finite-open topology, is unordered Baire-like.
item.dc:creator: Mar\'ia V. Ferrer, Salvador Hern\'andez, Isabel Sep\'ulveda

item.title: Banach Gelfand Triples with Kernel Theorems via Equivalence Bimodules
item.description: arXiv:2609.37780v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hilbert C*-modules whose coefficient C*-algebra is equipped with a finite faithful trace generate Banach Gelfand triples. This provides a natural setting for the interpretation of Hilbert C*-modules as function spaces. In particular, when the modules are finitely generated and projective, their external tensor products interact well with projective tensor products. This allowed us to derive abstract kernel theorems for Hilbert C*-modules. As an application, we apply our results to Heisenberg modules and obtain new kernel theorems for time-frequency analysis.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Bytchenkoff, Arvin Lamando, Franz Luef

item.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part II: Abstract Integration in Net Convergence Structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.21014v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The construction of a coherent and general integration procedure is the central question of this second part of our study of measure theory in convergence spaces. We define, and establish convergence theorems for such process of integration, called the net Riemann integration, in convergence groups and commutative monoids, preserving the prescribed convergence throughout. The underlying interchange theorem admits noncommutative groups and requires right completeness only at the cardinality of the error family. Under intrinsic stability assumptions, countable error control therefore needs only sequential completeness, even for arbitrary integration nets, from which we also stablish a general version of Henstock's lemma. The resulting uniform theorems reaches incomplete ranges in which no complete subspace contains a tail of the approximating integrals. In the ordered locally solid convergence theory side, countability of the inner direction replaces countable accessibility of the approximants, and local existence arguments yield monotone and dominated convergence and, under additional controller assumptions, a further extension through increasing integrable barriers with pointwise coverage and uniformly vanishing excess primitives. This constructs the limiting integral without a common integrable envelope and gives uniform control of primitive variation. We finish with two appendices on new and general results of abstract metrization of net convergences and related topics.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Reggiolli Teixeira

item.title: Linear Preservers of Semipositivity and Minimal Semipositivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.27413v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify all real linear into preservers of semipositivity on $M_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})$, $m,n\ge2$, relative to arbitrary source and target pairs of proper cones, without assuming invertibility or a prescribed form. The classification consists of product maps $L(A)=XAY$ and rank-$n$ degenerate maps $L(A)=\Psi(u^TA)$, subject to explicit cone and matrix-pencil conditions. For square minimal semipositivity with respect to the standard nonnegative orthant, preservation forces the operator to be invertible: for $n\ge2$, the linear into preservers are precisely the maps $L(A)=XAY$ and $L(A)=XA^TY$ with $X,Y\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ satisfying $X^{-1},Y^{-1}\ge0$. We also classify all linear preservers of orthant semipositivity from $M_{2,2}(\mathbb{R})$ to $M_{1,3}(\mathbb{R})$ into three disjoint classes, two of which consist of maps of rank three outside product form.
item.dc:creator: Yulong Tian, Jinli Xu

item.title: Additive preservers of mutual strong numerical radius orthogonality
item.description: arXiv:2610.39080v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with $\dim H\ge 2$. We characterize the nonzero additive maps on $\mathcal{B}(H)$ and on its self-adjoint part $\mathcal{B}_s(H)$ that preserve mutual strong numerical-radius orthogonality in one direction, assuming surjectivity only in infinite dimension. These maps are precisely those of the form $A\mapsto cUAU^*$, where $U$ is unitary or antiunitary, and $c$ is a nonzero complex scalar for $\mathcal{B}(H)$ and a nonzero real scalar for $\mathcal{B}_s(H)$.
item.dc:creator: Yulong Tian, Jinli Xu

item.title: Two-scale criteria for Poincar\'{e} and log-Sobolev inequalities with applications to Markov chain Monte Carlo
item.description: arXiv:2509.15410v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a collection of distributions $\{P_{y}\}$ and a mixing distribution $\rho$ supported over $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, we propose new sufficient conditions under which the mixture / joint distribution satisfies a Poincar\'{e} or log-Sobolev inequality. We develop these sufficient conditions in a unified manner using the framework of $\Phi$-Sobolev inequalities (Chafa\"{i}, 2004). The conditions that we develop in this work are satisfied by a variety of Markov chains, and consequently allows us to characterise the evolution of these functional inequalities for iterates generated by simulating these Markov chains.
