As a result, we obtain an clean error analysis for estimating a broad class of functionals using Markov chain Monte Carlo strategies along these Markov chains.
item.dc:creator: Vishwak Srinivasan

item.title: An explicit formula for the limit of the heat kernel measures on the spheres embedded in $\mathbb {R}^\infty$
item.description: arXiv:2510.25855v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the heat kernel measures based at the north pole of the spheres $S^{N-1}(\sqrt N)$, with a properly scaled radius $\sqrt N$ and adjusted center, in the sense of finite-dimensional marginals, to a Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^\infty$. In particular, in the direction of the base point, the variance of this limiting measure is $1-e^{-t}-te^{-t}$, and in the orthogonal directions, the variance is $1-e^{-t}$.
item.dc:creator: Minh-Luan Doan, Evan O'Dorney

item.title: Circular orders: topology and continuous actions
item.description: arXiv:2512.17314v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the topology of circularly ordered sets. While the algebraic notion is classical, the general topological theory has received comparatively little attention. In this work we provide a self-contained topological exposition and present several new directions and results. Our aim is to initiate a systematic study of generalized circularly ordered topological spaces and of continuous group actions on them. Provide a convex uniform structure description of circularly ordered compactifications. This yields a topological analysis of Novak's regular completion and its uniformity. Demonstrate that this uniform-structure approach yields several new results in the theory of $G$-compactifications for topological group actions on abstract ordered spaces. Reexamine functions of bounded variation on circularly ordered sets and prove generalizations of Helly's selection theorem (for circular and linear orders). These developments and the systematic analysis of circular order topologies are motivated by recent applications in topological dynamics, particularly in joint works with Eli Glasner.
item.dc:creator: Michael Megrelishvili

item.title: Taylor-Accelerated Neural Network Interpolation Operators on Irregular Grids: Higher-Order Approximation and Derivative-Informed Field Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2602.05589v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, a new class of Taylor-accelerated neural-network interpolation operators is introduced for quasi-uniform, irregularly distributed grids to reconstruct derivative-informed physical fields in both univariate and multivariate settings. The framework incorporates Taylor expansions within the neural network operators framework, allowing operators to efficiently utilize the smoothness of the target function. We determine the analytical properties of the proposed operators, including well-posedness, uniform boundedness, and exact interpolation at the sampling nodes. Additionally, we establish polynomial reproduction to a specified degree and provide Jackson-type error estimates based on higher-order moduli of smoothness, thereby improving convergence rates on quasi-uniform, irregular grids. The applicability of the method is demonstrated by reconstructing physical fields such as temperature, electromagnetic fields, and fluid properties, including pressure and velocity. The numerical results show that the proposed operators provide reliable, accurate estimates in the presence of noise and irregular sampling. The enhanced accuracy of the proposed method is validated by comparing it with current interpolation systems on irregular grids, including Lagrange-type methods.
item.dc:creator: Sachin Saini

item.title: Convexity of Radial Mean Bodies via an Extension of Ball's Bodies
item.description: arXiv:2603.14134v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we extend a classical theorem of Keith Ball on integrals of log-concave functions along rays against the weight $r^{p-1}$ to the previously inaccessible regime $p\in (-1,0)$: if $g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+$ is an integrable, upper semi-continuous, log-concave function which attains its maximum at the origin and has the origin in the interior of its support, then \[ x\mapsto \left(\frac{p}{g(o)}\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{p-1}(g(rx)-g(o))\mathrm{d}\,r\right)^{-\frac{1}{p}} \] is a gauge on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Our approach also provides a new proof of the original regime $p> 0$. The argument is based on a reduction to a two-dimensional inequality derived from Pr\'ekopa's theorem, which may be of independent interest. As a consequence of this extension, we resolve a nearly 30-year-old question of Richard Gardner and Gaoyong Zhang in the affirmative. In 1998, R. Gardner and G. Zhang introduced the radial $p$th mean bodies $R_p K$ of a convex body $K\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ for $p>-1$. Furthermore, they established that $R_p K$ is convex for $p\geq 0$, but the convexity of $R_p K$ for $p\in (-1,0)$ remained open. We prove that $R_p K$ is convex for all $p>-1$.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Langharst

item.title: Stable Initial-State Recovery from Dynamical Samples using Nagy-Type and Pollard-Hilding-Type Frame Perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2606.08066v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stimulated by Aldroubi and his collaborator's recent work on dynamical sampling, we consider a homogeneous discrete dynamical system of the form $f_n = A f_{n-1}= A^{n}f, \quad f_0 = f$, where A is a bounded linear operator on a separable Hilbert space H, which is known as the evolution operator, and $f_0 \in \mathcal{H}$ is the unknown initial state. The associated dynamical samples are given by the collection $\{\langle A^n f, g\rangle: g \in \mathcal{G, 0 \leq n < n < L(g)}\}$, where $\mathcal{G} \subset H$, is a finite or countable sampling set and $L$ is a function $L: G \rightarrow \mathbb{N} \bigcup \{\infty\}$. We analyze the stability of perturbed dynamical sampling systems in the sense of Nagy and Pollard-Hilding. More precisely, we establish sufficient conditions for the stable recovery of an initial state from perturbed dynamical samples obtained by changing the sampling vector, the evolution operator, ro simultaneously both, within the framework of Nagy-type and Pollard-Hilding-type perturbation of frames.
item.dc:creator: Ruchi, Lalit Kumar Vashisht

item.title: Optimal Condition Numbers in Low-Rank Positive Semidefinite Matrix Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2608.22418v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we focus on the stability of positive semidefinite matrix sensing maps $\Phi_{\mathcal{A}}=(\langle A_i,X\rangle)_{i=1}^m$ where $A_i\succeq 0$, $X\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r$. We introduce the bi-Lipschitz constants of $\Phi_{\mathcal{A}}$ and define the global condition numbers as the ratio of upper and lower Lipschitz constants. We give deterministic universal lower bounds for these condition numbers that depend only on the rank $r$ and on the underlying field. We then show that rank-one Gaussian measurements asymptotically attain these bounds, except for the operator-norm condition number over $\mathbb R$ when $r=1$. For this exceptional case, we establish a sharper universal lower bound and prove its asymptotic sharpness. As an application, we derive stability guarantees for an $\ell_1$-residual PhaseLift-type estimator at the optimal sampling scale. These results identify the intrinsic limits of conditioning in positive semidefinite matrix sensing and connect these limits to stable low-rank recovery.
item.dc:creator: Mingxuan Sun, Zhiqiang Xu

item.title: QWEP stability under twisted crossed products
item.description: arXiv:2610.03424v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the QWEP property of twisted crossed products and its relation to Fourier multiplier transference on noncommutative $L_p$-spaces. We show that QWEP is not preserved by crossed products of QWEP von Neumann algebras by hyperlinear groups. Our examples include trace-preserving actions of a torsion-free residually finite Kazhdan group on a diffuse abelian algebra and on the hyperfinite type II$_1$ factor. We also obtain non-QWEP crossed products with nontrivial scalar cocycles. For scalar twists, we prove that a finite trace-preserving crossed product is QWEP if and only if its ordinary crossed product and its twisted group von Neumann algebra are QWEP. In the positive direction, we establish a restriction theorem for scalar twists of regular wreath products. These results provide QWEP inputs for Fourier multiplier transference and identify a completely bounded multiplier norm obstruction to QWEP. Finally, operator-valued cocycles give finite QWEP crossed products whose acting groups are not hyperlinear.
item.dc:creator: Kai Zeng

item.title: Quantum integrals II: Dominated and almost uniform convergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.16499v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: One main aim of our paper is to formulate noncommutative versions of the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem in the setting of quantum integration theory on von Neumann algebras. Our starting point is a reformulation of classical dominated convergence in terms of weak* convergence. Using our recent sequential-continuity theorem, we obtain dominated convergence formulations for sequentially normal states and, under domination by a fixed bounded integrable majorant, for sequentially normal weights. Integrable, possibly unbounded, majorants are treated first in the tracial setting, then for arbitrary von Neumann algebras using Haagerup's \(L^1\) space, and finally using normal semifinite weights and their GNS representations. For any faithful normal semifinite weight phi, weak* convergence of norm-bounded sequences is characterized by `integrating against' bounded positive integrable majorants. We also study noncommutative almost uniform and local almost uniform convergence, and make the relationship with the order convergence results of Chetcuti et al. explicit. In particular, for norm-bounded sequences, local phi-bilaterally almost uniform convergence implies weak* convergence and \(\|h^{1/2}(x_n-x)h^{1/2}\|_1\to0\) for every positive Haagerup L1 density h, without assuming \(\sigma\)-finiteness. We also prove a dominated convergence theorem in the predual: fixed positive order domination and Petz's almost uniform convergence imply convergence in the predual norm. We establish implications and equivalences among these convergence notions, connecting dominated convergence with tracial and nontracial integration.
item.dc:creator: David P. Blecher

item.title: A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.26478v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a detailed, direct proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the first-order Gaussian vector Riesz transform, using the fractional obstacle method of Ouyang, Spector, and Stockdale. For $d\gamma_n=\pi^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^2}\,dx$, let $L=-\tfrac12\Delta+x\cdot\nabla$, $D=2^{-1/2}\nabla$, and $R_\gamma=DL^{-1/2}\Pi_0$, where $\Pi_0$ removes the mean. We prove that $R_\gamma$ has weak-type constant at most $2$ on real-valued inputs, independently of $n$. The main construction is the unique unshifted decomposition $F=g+L^{1/2}u$, for nonnegative $F\in L^2(\gamma_n)$ and $a>\int F\,d\gamma_n$, with $u\geq0$, $\min\{F,a\}\leq g\leq a$, preservation of mass, and $g=a$ on $\{u>0\}$. We retain the details of coercivity, the Lewy--Stampacchia estimate, the upgrade from the form domain to the operator domain, and locality. We also identify the $L^1$ extension with the principal-value transform and obtain the constant $8/\pi$ for complex-valued inputs.
item.dc:creator: Cristian E. Guti\'errez, Juan Manfredi

item.title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
item.description: arXiv:2610.39967v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.
item.dc:creator: Kaiwen Yang
